blocks.text: Real Russian sentences that use what the lesson teaches. Type the missing word, or pick it, until it turns green.

These are real sentences: from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR), with their English translations, and from the public-domain Russian books in this library, with author and title. Each blank is the word the sentence really has; the word in brackets is its dictionary form.

exercises.q: This isn't any old chair; it's an antique.
exercises.ru: Это не ___ там старый стул, а раритет.
exercises.why: «In general, the particle "-нибудь" implies complete indefiniteness; the particle "-то" implies some degree of certainty.» a) In interrogative and imperative sentences use -нибудь. b) In positive statements referring to the past or present use -то. — DLI, Lesson 59. Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
